But no matter how much an underage child likes someone, that is as far as it can go.

In times when the future is uncertain, who has the capacity to carry someone else's future?

Wen Ni cried very bitterly that day.

It wasn't because Shen Huaixu had left; the primary cause was clearly that she had lost her homework notebook, and her homeroom teacher had said it would be fine if she was just more careful next time.

But Wen Zhiwen had rushed over from his company, and without even asking for the reason, he had berated her right in front of everyone in the office.

Everyone was watching her.

Wen Ni felt like she couldn't breathe.

She felt like a monkey in a zoo, being teased and gawked at by the crowd.

Under the weight of her intense self-esteem, she really couldn't hold it together.

She whispered, begging Wen Zhiwen to stop.

But not only did he not stop, he raised his voice even higher, scolding her until she couldn't even lift her head.

Even people passing by were looking inside.

It wasn't until the homeroom teacher couldn't stand it anymore and closed the office door that Wen Ni finally let out a breath.

But had she really let out a breath?

No.

She stood there, her hands and feet cold, her whole body trembling. She just wanted to leave that office entirely.

She didn't care how, as long as her father, Wen Zhiwen, could just shut his mouth for a moment.

Even just for one minute would have been enough!

But it seemed that God never listened to her on this matter.

Wen Zhiwen went from hurling insults to claiming that he shouldn't have had her as a daughter in the first place.

When this heavy, cruel sentence fell, even the homeroom teacher had to step in to try and persuade him otherwise.

Everyone in the world knows that some things should not be said.

But not Wen Zhiwen.

He believed he was the master of this household, and he had the right to criticize anyone in it.

He could not tolerate his daughter failing to even finish her homework.

Because he was the most outstanding young man from their village.

Wen Ni didn't remember where the breakdown began.

It seemed like someone started to comfort her.

Actually, sometimes she became numb and didn't feel aggrieved anymore.

But it is precisely when someone comforts you that it becomes the most unbearable.

Wen Ni had strong self-esteem, so she couldn't just laugh this off and move on.

When Wen Zhiwen followed her out of the office, he looked down at her from the top of the stairs once more.

"Wen Ni, I don't want to be called to school for such trivial matters ever again. You only make me lose face! I spent so much money to send you to this school, and this is how you repay me? If there is a next time, I won't have a daughter like you; I’d rather spend that money on your cousin."

Wen Zhiwen was unlucky; he had caught the tail end of the one-child policy.

Wen Ni could only be his only daughter.

He wanted a son, a son as outstanding as himself, to inherit his mantle and his perfect genes.

Wen Ni had clearly lost from the start based on her gender.

Having grown up hearing these words, Wen Ni’s breakdown was only accelerated by Wen Zhiwen saying this in front of so many classmates.

She didn't return to the classroom.

She hid in the corner of a flower bed to cry.

She thought there would be no one there.

But why, for heaven's sake, was someone still having a PE class?

It was a rainy day!

Until a pair of white sneakers appeared before her eyes.

Wen Ni looked up, and Jian Yuchen stuffed a pack of pink tissues into her hand before walking away with his hands in his pockets.

Where did she throw that pack of tissues?

She never used them anyway.

But she remembered the pattern was quite pretty.

She didn't know how someone like Jian Yuchen could have chosen such a cute pattern.

However, he had caught her in such a humiliating moment, and Wen Ni didn't want to think about it.

Every time she thought of that scene, she felt like Jian Yuchen was a demon who had peered into the depths of her soul.

She was terrified that he would use this incident to mock her.

Fortunately, up until now in their marriage, Jian Yuchen had never mentioned that rainy day.

Perhaps because she was in a bad mood in her dream, Wen Ni felt a bit dazed when she was patted awake by Jian Yuchen.

The man's handsome face was very close, and his large palm was still patting her face. "Wen Ni, wake up!"

"What are you doing?" Wen Ni felt her face aching from his slaps.

"Are you looking for an excuse to commit domestic violence by pretending to wake me up?" Wen Ni covered her face and sat up.

Jian Yuchen replied irritably, "Look at the tears you shed; you've soaked the pillow."

When the man said this, his face was dark. "And you kept calling out 'Shen Huaixu.' What's the matter? Want to relive the old days, do you?"

Jian Yuchen had gotten up the moment he heard her call the first time.

Then he sat at the head of the bed, watching her cry and call out in her sleep, his heart feeling as blocked as if it were filled with stones.

Wen Ni was surprised. "I was calling Shen Huaixu in my dream?"

"Yeah," he squeezed the tone out of his throat in a nasty voice.

It was as sour as if he’d been soaked in a vat of vinegar.

Wen Ni rubbed her hair. "You must have heard wrong. I didn't see Shen Huaixu in my dream at all."

It was all Wen Zhiwen!

Jian Yuchen sneered, "My ears are fine. It’s clear who is trying to cover things up."

Listen to that—sarcastic and moody first thing in the morning.

Wen Ni pouted. "Believe what you want."

She went to get up, clutching her waist. "Are you a beast? Why did you treat me so roughly? Are you settling a private grudge?"

"Me? Treat you roughly?" Jian Yuchen directly unbuttoned his shirt collar.

Wen Ni leaned back defensively. "What are you doing!"

The man pulled it open, revealing various pinch marks and bite marks on his chest.

"Who exactly treated who roughly? Do you want to see for yourself if there's a single patch of good skin left on me?"

"This... didn't I do this, right?" Wen Ni hesitated, feeling a bit uncertain.

"Heh, you drank two cups of swill and didn't know north from south. One moment you said you were a mushroom, the next a little daisy, and later you said you were a cup of milk tea, telling me not to spill you."

"And telling me to make sure the straw was inserted correctly."

???

What kind of nonsense are you spouting!

Impossible! Absolutely not—

**

chapters.title: What’s So Strange About Not Liking an Ex-Boyfriend
chapters.content:
As for Wen Ni’s habit of refusing to admit when she’s done something wrong, as her husband, Jian Yuchen was already used to it.

Wen Ni was also muttering to herself, because she felt that, well, this sort of thing... she wasn't, um, incapable of doing it.

Thinking of this, Wen Ni scratched her head.

That shouldn't be; I'm not that kind of person...

Anyway, she stuck to one principle: never admit it.

How could Jian Yuchen not know what she was thinking?

When he took out his phone, Wen Ni’s eyelids twitched.

She suddenly threw off the quilt and jumped up to grab his phone.

Jian Yuchen leaned back, and while turning, he cranked the phone's volume to the maximum.

Wen Ni’s voice echoed throughout the room.

"No, no, I'm a little mushroom!"

"Is it milk tea or a mushroom?"

"Why do you have a mushroom? Wow, you stole my mushroom, give me back my cap!"

"..."

Wen Ni’s face turned bright red instantly. Furious, she jumped up and scrambled onto Jian Yuchen’s back. "Give it back to me! Give it back! Delete it!"

Jian Yuchen reached out and caught her thighs, saying irritably, "Can you put some clothes on?"

It was early in the morning; he couldn't handle this stimulation.

Were they going to work or not?

Wen Ni knew that, but it wasn't like he hadn't seen it before!

"Heh, you don't want to look now? You're usually unhappy when I wear clothes, so what are you pretending for?"

Jian Yuchen closed his eyes. "What, do you want neither of us to go to work?"

"So what? You delete the recording first."

"No, I’m planning to record a video too, to see how Director Wen sexually harasses me."

"Jian Yuchen, you shameless man!"

After all the fuss, Jian Yuchen didn't arrive at the office until 10:00 AM.

But since he was the externally hired boss, who dared to say anything about him being late?

It was just that, why did there seem to be suspicious red marks under his suit collar...

Could those be... hickeys?

Because Jian Yuchen was late, the meeting that was supposed to be at 9:00 AM was pushed to 10:30 AM.

Originally, no one would have been able to see what was under his collar.

But as it happened, the air conditioning in the conference room wasn't on at the start, and Jian Yuchen pulled at his collar with one hand.

A row of hickeys was sucked under his collar...

What Jian Yuchen couldn't see was that his expressionless employees were tapping their thumbs on their phones at the speed of a rhythm game master.

[Did you see that? A whole string of them. So Simon likes wild little kittens!]

[Whoa, am I the only one who wants to know if it was a man or a woman?]

[Don't say it, it's all very shippable!]

[Eat something good while you can; you'd better still be able to "ship" it when he rejects your proposal later.]

[I can do it! Hit me, Simon!]

[...]

It wasn't until the meeting ended and Ning Yan followed him back to his office and closed the door that Jian Yuchen revealed his true colors.

"After the party broke up last night, where did you go to have such a good time?"

Jian Yuchen glanced at him. "Speak like a human; I don't understand."

Ning Yan poked his neck with his finger. "If you're going to sneak a snack, at least clean up first."

"Everyone outside has been watching the show all morning. Where did you find that girl? She's too ferocious. But then again, at your age, you should be considering settling down."

Hearing this, Jian Yuchen opened his phone camera and finally saw the good work Wen Ni had done.

Heh, where did he find her?

She was the director that you, Ning Yan, personally recruited.

"Doing it openly and aboveboard—what do you mean by 'sneaking around'? Do you even know how to use words?" Jian Yuchen said with disdain.

He sleeps with Wen Ni legally and legitimately.

What is this?

This is a legal hickey.

It’s nothing like those illicit ones others have.

Ning Yan couldn't win the argument, so he said, "Fine. I think there’s still a chance with Jinfeng. Wen Ni took the morning off; let’s have a meeting with the three of us when she arrives this afternoon. I plan to have someone from the planning department go on the business trip with her."

Jian Yuchen paused. "Go to Jinfeng?"

"Yes. Since the client isn't satisfied, we have to make them satisfied before they’ll willingly open their wallets, right? We only have two major projects this year, and I’m not willing to lose this one."

"Then clear your schedule. I’m going too."

Ning Yan raised an eyebrow. "Didn't you just get back from a business trip?"

"So what? If the company’s business makes money, I get a cut. Besides, Wen Ni isn't suited for socializing."

She is better suited to be a simple, pure designer.

Ning Yan thought for a moment. "We'll discuss it in the meeting this afternoon."

"Suit yourself."

Jian Yuchen opened his computer, then noticed Ning Yan was still sitting there. "Anything else?"

"I was just about to ask you—when did you and Wen Ni start living in the same residential complex? How come I didn't know? You two never mentioned it."

Jian Yuchen looked at his screen. "I was just messing with Shen Huaixu last night."

"I thought so. If you two were in the same complex, the property management group chat would have exploded. President Shen is a decent guy; do you have a problem with him?"

If that were the case, Ning Yan would have to consider preventing any possibility of indirect contact between the two.

A problem?

He had a huge problem.

Jian Yuchen couldn't reconcile with Wen Ni's first love.

And he couldn't bring himself to pretend to coexist peacefully with him just for the sake of a little money.

"Yeah, a bit. I won't be involved in any business that requires direct contact with him from now on. I’ll handle the Wen Ni side of things."

"No way. You’d rather deal with Wen Ni than Shen Huaixu? *Tsk*, your attitude makes me a bit suspicious about what’s going on between you two."

Jian Yuchen replied, "Did you change careers to become the village gossip center?"

"Fine, fine. Ask you two questions and I get chewed out. See you at noon."

Ning Yan got up and left.

Jian Yuchen rubbed his temples. Just thinking about the way that stubborn girl Wen Ni looked at him—as if he were an eyesore—made his teeth itch.

Wen Ni woke up at noon, sneezed twice, and successfully discovered something.

She had a fever.

Afterward, she sent a message to Jian Yuchen, venting her anger.

*Wen Buding: It’s all your fault, all your fault! I have a fever!*

*Simon: There’s medicine in the small kit, in the third drawer on the right inside the cabinet behind the sofa.*

*Wen Buding: I have such a robust physique, yet I’m sick. Jian Yuchen, you must have sabotaged me! There’s treachery in the workplace, but I never expected to be caught off guard at home. You actually stabbed me in the back!*

*Simon: I must reiterate: last night I was sharpening my blade and cleaning my gun, single-handedly and invincible, engaging in a battle of wits and tongues without shedding blood, and finally putting the weapon away amidst the smoke of battle. Please don't describe such a scene of flying bullets and artillery fire as something so sneaky.*

*Wen Buding: ???*

*Wen Buding: Are you playing a game of idiom solitaire here?!*

*Simon: Take your medicine. Lunch is in the fridge; heat it up in the microwave yourself. If you can't, order takeout—get porridge. Do you need me to ask for more leave for you this afternoon?*

*Wen Buding: No need, I'll be at work later.*

Jian Yuchen knew she was a workaholic once she got busy.

He couldn't stop her.

He simply got up and went downstairs.

When Wen Ni took her medicine and arrived at the underground garage, she noticed Jian Yuchen’s R8 was gone. She then remembered he had left his car at the company yesterday and must have driven Ning Yan’s car back this morning.

Wen Ni took a taxi to the office. As soon as she entered, she saw a bouquet of roses, and finally, she found a thermos on her desk. A faint scent of ginger soup wafted through the air.

**

chapters.title: Wen Ni is Very Good
chapters.content:
Wen Ni put down her bag, looked at the roses first, then picked up the thermos.

She sent a message to Jian Yuchen.

*Wen Buding: Don't think you can save our precarious marriage with ginger soup and roses! I’m not that easy to bribe!*

*Simon: ?*

*Simon: Who gave you the roses?*

Even the punctuation was gone.

Could it be that Jian Yuchen didn't send them?

Wen Ni rummaged through the flowers and found a card.

*[Looking forward to our collaboration. Shen Huaixu.]*

...

Wen Ni immediately felt the card in her hand was like a hot potato and tossed it aside.

Damn it, she had actually handed evidence over to Jian Yuchen.

Zhou Xueli knocked and entered with a mischievous grin. "Oh my, I was about to burst since you weren't here this morning. Jian Yuchen is definitely acting weird."

Wen Ni pushed the flowers aside. "What’s wrong with him now? Did he bite a client?"

Zhou Xueli handed her a document. "Nonono~ There’s a hickey on his neck. You can only imagine how hard the other person must have sucked."

"Cough, cough..." Wen Ni took a sip of ginger tea and closed her eyes comfortably. "Maybe it was a mite bite."

"Forget it. Since when did you start playing the innocent card? That line doesn't fit—delete it and say it again."

Thinking of how her waist still ached from last night, Wen Ni put down the thermos and said, "You guys seem pretty free. Is there nothing else to discuss in this company besides Jian Yuchen’s gossip?"

"What else is there? Does Jameson two-timing and getting cornered by his girlfriend at the office door count?"

Wen Ni had a look of confusion. "Why didn't I receive such exciting news immediately?"

"You didn't check the group chat this morning? I thought you were lurking." Zhou Xueli glanced at the roses on the desk. "Also, everyone is guessing who is chasing you again."

Wen Ni shrugged. "Just a client. Nothing about chasing."

Zhou Xueli leaned back in her chair. "Looks like this one doesn't have much of a chance."

Otherwise, Wen Ni would have definitely put these flowers in a vase.

Didn't the internet say that roses are for fooling young girls, and in the world of adults, we only have camellias and earning money to spend on ourselves?

"Alright, I'm going back to my desk, or I'll get a barrage of calls if I'm not found."

Once Zhou Xueli left, Wen Ni finally felt a moment of quiet for her muddled brain.

Ning Yan called and asked her to come upstairs.

Lately, the probability of running into Jian Yuchen in Ning Yan’s office was too high, and Wen Ni couldn't help but glance at him several times.

As it turned out, that jerk Jian Yuchen was expressionless and didn't even spare her a glance.

Fine, playing the cold and aloof card today, are we?

Wen Ni looked away. "A business trip? Didn't you say we were going to Jinfeng this afternoon?"

"Yes, we added Simon to the trip last minute. Anyway, you don't have any urgent cases on hand, so let's go together and close the deal."

Wen Ni shrugged. "I'm fine with that."

"Then it's settled."

The two left the office one after the other.

Jian Yuchen didn't give her a look either. Wen Ni thought this guy was acting strange today.

They walked to the elevator, and a colleague passed by.

"Simon, Winnie~"

Both nodded in unison, then entered the elevator as if they didn't know each other.

Given the way they were always on the verge of arguing, no one else wanted to get in the elevator.

Otherwise, anyone caught in the middle would end up trying to break up a fight and getting no thanks for it.

Wen Ni thought he would at least apologize for giving her a cold last night, but he acted as if she owed him a million.

Just as she was cursing him in her heart, Jian Yuchen suddenly spoke, "Dad said we should go home for dinner tonight."

Wen Ni nodded before realizing, "Which dad?"

"Your dad."

It was the one thing she didn't want to happen. Her disgust for her original family made Wen Ni feel stifled at the mere thought of going home.

Perhaps seeing her momentary daze, Jian Yuchen’s tone softened. "Did you drink the ginger soup?"

Wen Ni snapped back to reality. "Yeah."

She looked like a wilted eggplant.

Jian Yuchen wanted to say, "What are you afraid of? I'll be there with you," but the elevator doors opened.

They didn't have time to say anything, and Wen Ni walked out of the elevator like a ghost.

Jian Yuchen returned to his office, wanting to send her something, but figured she wouldn't be in the mood to reply.

He decided to wait until after work.

Wen Ni was indeed not in the right state of mind that afternoon. Coupled with the dream from last night, she felt irritable at the thought of going home and facing Wen Zhiwen.

But the hands on the clock kept turning.

After work, Wen Ni found her car. After they both drove home separately, she didn't even have time to change her clothes before hopping into the passenger seat of the R8.

"I’ve already bought fruit and drinks. Is there anything else you need to bring?"

"Oh, thanks." Wen Ni really wasn't in the mood.

Jian Yuchen frowned, wanting to say something, but Wen Ni suddenly opened her bag, took out a cushion compact, and looked at herself. "Is my makeup too heavy today?"

"No."

"Is the lipstick too bright?"

"Isn't it the usual bean paste color?"

"I guess."

Wen Ni took a deep breath. "Let's go."

Death comes sooner or later.

If they were late, she’d just get scolded.

Better to bite the bullet and go early.

The old residential complex where her family lived was hard to park in. Years ago, Wen Zhiwen had saved money but didn't buy a house, just watching the housing prices in H City skyrocket to astronomical levels.

Thinking that there was an old vegetable market and old shops nearby, and that selling this house wouldn't allow them to buy anything in a better location, he just stayed put.

Wen Ni grew up here. One trip home, and she ran into an acquaintance every five steps.

Just greeting them made her face stiffen from smiling.

"Wen Ni is back, huh?"

"Yeah."

"You two are such a lovely couple."

"Heh heh."

Just as they reached the door, they could smell the aroma coming from the kitchen.

There were two pairs of slippers at the door.

"Yuchen is here!" Jiang Meili called out from the kitchen. "Old Wen, the kids are here."

In the living room, Wen Zhiwen put down his newspaper. "They're here, so they're here. Do I have to go out and welcome them personally?"

Despite saying that, he was already walking out.

Wen Ni felt like a toad being stared at by a snake. She swallowed hard. "Dad."

"Why are you so timid when you greet people!" Wen Zhiwen glared at her, then smiled at Jian Yuchen. "You brought things again. Didn't I tell you not to be so polite last time?"

"That’s only right. Mom is in the kitchen; I’ll go help."

"Don't. That’s not work for a man. Wen Ni, you go. Now that you’re married, you should act like a wife. Every time you come over, you let Yu Chen bring so many things; if people find out, they’ll only say you have no manners."

Wen Ni desperately wanted to retort, but the words stuck in her throat and she swallowed them back.

Anyway, everything she did was wrong; after all these years, she had become numb to it.

"Dad, I’m the one who says Wen Ni has a good temper. If it were up to me, I wouldn't have been able to find a wife. Don't go scaring her away."

Wen Ni paused and turned her head. Jian Yuchen smiled as he put the items away, then raised an eyebrow and said, "Take my coat to your room and hang it up."

Wen Zhiwen huffed, "You, you just know how to say nice things. Do you think I don't know her? Just don't go to your house and embarrass me."

"Wen Ni is very good, Dad. She is very good." Jian Yuchen repeated it twice, not letting go of the hand he was holding, then turned and said, "Well? Go on."

Wen Ni pursed her lips, took his coat, and quickly retreated into the room.

Only when she closed the door did she feel the suffocating air begin to circulate.

chapters.title: Jian Yuchen, I Don't Like This Home
chapters.content:
Even inside the room, listening to Wen Zhiwen’s voice outside, Wen Ni felt as if a giant hand were gripping her heart, thrashing about in her chest and leaving her unable to breathe.

She leaned her back against the door, closed her eyes, and took another deep breath.

She had done this so often since arriving that it had become second nature.

She didn't want to go back out; she even recoiled at the thought of facing Wen Zhiwen.

"Wen Ni, what are you doing in the room?"

The door was knocked. No sooner had Wen Zhiwen called out to her than he was inviting Jian Yuchen to drink.

Wen Ni let out a heavy sigh and opened the door to come out.

Wen Zhiwen had been all smiles just a moment ago, but upon seeing her, he immediately said, "Yu Chen is here, and you have nothing to do? Hiding in the room doing nothing? You’re just going to embarrass me. What will people think of the daughter I raised?"

"..." Wen Ni didn't make a sound, because if she talked back, the outcome would certainly be that she wouldn't be eating this meal at all.

Wen Zhiwen would flip the table.

In this house, Wen Zhiwen’s authority was not to be challenged.

Otherwise, she would be subjected to cold violence for the entire coming year.

Sometimes Wen Ni wanted to tell herself to stand up to him, to shout until he realized his daughter wasn't made of dough.

But in the end, for her mother’s sake, she had to keep coming back to this house.

Wen Ni had always felt that she had grown up without wanting for food or clothing, and she didn't feel she had ever lacked anything compared to others.

Yet, she would always remember the first time she brought Jian Yuchen home.

She had envied the atmosphere between him and his parents so much.

That was the first time she had felt inferior.

She hated losing face in front of others, but it seemed as if Wen Zhiwen derived pleasure from lecturing her.

If he were like this to everyone, Wen Ni would have nothing to say.

But he was always a hundred times better to other people's children than to his own.

Wen Ni still remembered when she won first prize in the city-wide painting competition and came home full of joy. Wen Zhiwen had simply tossed the certificate aside. "What’s the use of this competition? Can painting put food on the table? You only know how to mess with these useless things, which is why your grades don't improve."

He was always high and mighty.

He could always extinguish her enthusiasm with a bucket of cold water.

Then he would tell her that she was a useless waste, that she would never be as good as others.

The stain on Wen Zhiwen’s life was that he hadn't fathered a son like himself.

"The child has finally come home, why are you saying such things? Wen Ni, Mom made the shiitake mushroom and chestnut chicken you love. Come over and eat."

Wen Ni wasn't in the mood and walked past Wen Zhiwen.

The atmosphere in the house suddenly turned cold because of Wen Zhiwen’s words.

"Now that your wings are stiff, you can't even be told a few words."

Wen Zhiwen sat down with a thud, but Jian Yuchen suddenly spoke up, "Dad, Wen Ni has been very tired from work lately, so please don't lecture her."

Wen Zhiwen, having lost face, took a sip of his drink with an expressionless face. "Eat!"

Jiang Meili smiled and said, "Yu Chen, did you get a tan on this business trip? You look a bit thinner. You young people work and always drink that coffee or whatever; it’s bad for your health. You should sleep when you can, don't stay up late."

Jian Yuchen smiled and replied, "Yes, Mom. Once this busy period is over, I’m planning to take Wen Ni on a trip for a while to relax. Would you like to come with us then?"

Jiang Meili’s eyes crinkled with a smile. "I won't go. We have calligraphy classes at the senior university, and I have to attend. You two just go yourselves."

Jian Yuchen looked at Wen Ni, who was keeping her head down to eat. "Alright, we’ll bring you back some souvenirs."

"You young people just love buying random things. It’s better to save some money; earning it isn't easy."

Wen Zhiwen snorted coldly, "Buying all sorts of junk, just getting scammed by those 'Peach' or 'Orange' sites online."

"Dad, that’s called Taobao. E-commerce is popular now, and life is all about quick payments. Things online aren't necessarily bad."

"Yu Chen, don't always spoil her."

At this, Wen Zhiwen, smelling of alcohol, tapped the table. "Wen Ni."

Wen Ni raised her eyes, and Wen Zhiwen frowned as he scrutinized her. "You and Yu Chen have been married for two or three years now. Have you thought about when you’re going to have children?"

"Your mother and I have time now. If you have a child early, we can help you raise it. A woman should prioritize her family! You stay up day and night; when will you ever give birth to a big, healthy boy?"

The string in her brain snapped.

Wen Ni dropped her chopsticks and, under Wen Zhiwen’s dissatisfied gaze, said slowly, "I don't want to have children. I’m not ready to be a mother yet, and in any case, I’m not considering it for the next few years."

Her career was still on the rise; she was unwilling to sacrifice that to have a child right now.

Besides, she felt she wouldn't be good at raising a child.

Not to mention leaving a child for Wen Zhiwen to raise.

Wasn't one Wen Ni enough? Did she need to produce another little Wen Ni who inherited Wen Zhiwen’s bad temper?

She would go crazy!

Sure enough, Wen Zhiwen’s patriarchal authority could not be challenged. Upon hearing this, he slammed his chopsticks down. "Are you trying to rebel?!"

"You’re not an emperor, what rebellion? Isn't whether I have children or not my own business?" Wen Ni had truly had enough.

She didn't want to conflict with him, so why was it always endless!?

Wen Ni felt she couldn't speak properly to Wen Zhiwen at all.

Part of her personality was inherited from his tendency to bully those close to him and his sharp-tongued nature.

This made her hate Wen Zhiwen, and it made her hate herself for being like him.

"Dad!" Jian Yuchen suddenly spoke up, interrupting their conversation.

"It’s my fault."

"Yu Chen, don't speak up for her!"

"No, it really is my fault. I believe we are still young, and it’s not the time for children."

"Young? You’re both nearly 30, how is that young? By the time she’s an older mother, do you still think you’re kids? You need to have them early so you can have more."

"I’m full." Wen Ni stood up immediately and headed for the door.

"You get back here! I haven't finished talking, where are you going?!"

Behind her was a scene of chaos. Wen Ni ran down the stairs and walked straight ahead as soon as she exited the building, following whatever path lay before her.

Her mind was a blur until footsteps sounded behind her and she was pulled into a man’s embrace. Only then did Wen Ni stop.

"Wen Ni." Jian Yuchen’s voice was slightly breathless. She pursed her lips and remained silent.

"Alright, it’s okay now."

"No, it’s not okay." She turned her head and muttered, "I shouldn't have come back. I’m so annoyed, I shouldn't have come back!"

"We won't come back next time. We’ll just spend the weekend at home, hmm?"

The man was surprisingly good-tempered at this moment.

Wen Ni’s sharp thorns softened. "Jian Yuchen, I don't like this home."

While resisting Wen Zhiwen, she also felt guilty toward her parents.

She wanted to speak nicely, too, but why could she never manage it?

Even if she lowered her head and went along with Wen Zhiwen, he would always have a hundred reasons to tell her she wasn't—

chapters.title: You Don't Not Want to Eat, Do You?
chapters.content:
"I know."

Wen Ni buried her face in his chest, likely feeling that the sudden outburst of emotion made it impossible for her to remain calm in front of Jian Yuchen, so she pursed her lips and said, "I’m fine."

"Mm, I know you’re fine."

It’s good for people to vent their emotions.

Once vented, they can eventually calm down.

It’s better than bottling it up; if you bottle it up for too long, you’ll get sick.

Wen Ni had a powerful ability to heal.

All her bad moods stemmed from this family; as long as that wasn't touched, she could handle any problem in life.

In fact, Wen Zhiwen underestimated his daughter.

Jian Yuchen couldn't understand Wen Zhiwen’s thoughts or his way of doing things.

But there were many families around him similar to Wen Ni’s.

However, he also remembered that before they registered their marriage, Wen Zhiwen had pulled him aside to drink a lot.

At that dinner table, he had been drunk and said to him, "Yu Chen, I like you as a kid, so I’m very satisfied that Wen Ni chose you as her husband."

"My daughter is rebellious by nature; she hasn't listened to me since she was little."

"I don't know how to get along with her, and I don't know how to say nice things."

"You have to treat her well. She has a bad temper and a stubborn personality, so please be patient with her."

A man like Wen Zhiwen, who never bowed his head to anyone, had used words like "please" and "be patient" with him that night.

Even though Wen Ni was indeed not a son in his eyes, nor as excellent as he had hoped, Wen Zhiwen likely wanted the best for her.

Jian Yuchen wasn't sure about his own thoughts.

He couldn't say the phrase "there are no bad parents in the world" to Wen Ni either.

After all, not everyone has the ability to be a good parent.

Wen Ni was an adult now; she had her own judgment.

Therefore, Jian Yuchen didn't want to keep picking at the issue of her original family, tearing open wounds that already existed.

All he could do was stand up when she was questioned, despised, and doubted by Wen Zhiwen, and firmly tell Wen Zhiwen that Wen Ni was very good and please not to talk about her like that.

He didn't know how much Wen Zhiwen could take in.

At the very least, he shouldn't bully his wife like that.

Regardless of whether his original intention was good or bad.

"Let’s go." Jian Yuchen felt that Director Wen needed him to make the call now: were they leaving or not?

Wen Ni was indeed very docile as she let him put his arm around her and lead her to the car.

"You didn't eat your fill, did you?" As soon as Wen Ni left the residential complex, she was back to her lively self.

Jian Yuchen raised an eyebrow. "Hmm... what else do you want to eat?"

She really hadn't had much of an appetite earlier.

Wen Ni pointed ahead. "There’s a 30-year-old grilled fish shop over there. I used to bring my classmates here all the time; the flavor is very authentic."

As she spoke, she gave a thumbs-up, afraid Jian Yuchen wouldn't believe her.

Jian Yuchen nodded, his lips curling into a smile. "Oh, so you never brought me here?"

Wen Ni said uncomfortably, "Who told you to always talk back to me?"

Oh, so a man who talks back isn't qualified to eat grilled fish.

Truly, a classic "Wen-ism."

Wen Ni felt a little bit guilty, but only a tiny bit!

Not a drop more!

The shop really wasn't far; it was right at the street corner. At this hour, it was so crowded that three tables had already been set up under the awning outside.

They served not only grilled fish but also barbecue and crayfish.

Right next door were a cold drink shop and a stir-fry joint.

At the entrance stood three large red cylindrical tubs with tubes inserted into them; they were likely for keeping the crayfish.

Wen Ni was indeed hungry; the moment she saw them, she thought of the taste of spicy crayfish paired with lobster sauce.

"There's a small parking lot ahead, but it's private and charges a fee."

Anyway, Jian Yuchen was rich; she wasn't going to save money for him.

Mainly, there was absolutely no place to park in the old town area. If they didn't park there, they’d just be waiting for a parking ticket.

After informing him, Wen Ni parked the car. She had already grabbed her bag when she turned around, and Jian Yuchen saw her movements the moment he stepped out of the passenger seat.

"You're bringing a bag just for a meal?" The man gestured for her to put that heavy tote bag back in the car.

Wen Ni clicked her tongue. "I spent so much money on this bag, of course I’m going to carry it out. What if I need to touch up my makeup or something?"

Jian Yuchen, who had never actually seen her touch up her makeup except when she was at the company or attending business functions...

Fine. He would probably never understand the user manual for women in his entire life.

"Don't look at how many late-night snack spots there are on this street; there aren't many that are actually good. They're either too salty or too spicy. This Old Yu’s grilled fish is truly a masterpiece. You have to trust my taste."

When Wen Ni recommended something to others, she was always beaming, terrified that they wouldn't buy into her suggestion.

If they didn't, she would be very disappointed.

Jian Yuchen watched her, suddenly remembering that year when summer vacation had just started in their senior year of high school.

Everyone acted as if they had just been released from prison.

You could run into classmates at every major mall and KTV.

It was always the same few people coming and going.

Especially when they took off their school uniforms; it was like a fashion show, everyone eager to dress up and show off.

They would jump from one private room to another.

Wen Ni was like a celebrity at a fan meet-and-greet.

Singing from here to there.

What was he doing back then?

He seemed to have been dragged out of the house by his classmates.

He didn't really want to go when he reached the entrance of the complex.

It was only after hearing them say over the phone, "Just come! Wang Xiaohui, Jiang Yuyu, and Wen Ni from Class 7 are all there. It’s finally vacation and you’re still at home doing homework? Are you kidding me?"

Jian Yuchen had actually wanted to go play ice hockey.

Hearing that, he had asked for the address as if possessed.

What song was she singing back then?

Oh, one by a popular Taiwanese female singer—now just a memory of the past.

He and Wen Ni had grown up, too.

But the little girl who insisted that everyone had to go see a certain horror movie hadn't changed.

The summer heat was sweltering.

Having just stepped out of the air-conditioned car, beads of sweat appeared on the tip of her nose after only a few steps.

She was chattering away, and Jian Yuchen suddenly felt an itch in his throat.

He suddenly stopped walking.

Wen Ni stood still, guarded. "What? Don't tell me you don't want to eat anymore!"

If he suddenly didn't want to eat, she would definitely lose her temper.

Jian Yuchen said, "Come here."

Wen Ni was stunned, then slowly shuffled over. "What for?"

The man suddenly leaned down and kissed her.

Fortunately, it was just on the side of the road.

A dragonfly-skimming-the-water kind of kiss.

Wen Ni was enveloped by his frame; she couldn't really see anything.

She could only feel his broad shoulders blocking most of her view.

Under the shade of the trees, amidst the chirping of summer cicadas.

Amidst the smoke and bustle of the city, he kissed her.

He still had that familiar woody scent of cologne on him.

Wen Ni had done so many intimate things with him; she didn't even know how many times they had been to bed together.

But a kiss like this, devoid of any lust, actually made her blush.

"Why did you kiss me out of the blue?"

"Just felt like it."

He stared at her and suddenly smiled, revealing a sharp canine tooth.

Wen Ni suddenly remembered their first kiss.

To be honest, the memory wasn't great when she thought about it now.

Her first kiss with him was in their second year of high school—a terrible kiss.

He had chipped her dental retainer, and she had bumped him until his gums bled.

Could that even count as a kiss?

Wen Ni wasn't even sure, because after all, the accident rate was 98%.

chapters.title: This Taoist Priest... Are You Here to Exorcise Demons?
chapters.content:
"Why are you blushing?" Jian Yuchen wondered.

After all, with Wen Ni’s personality, she only blushed when she was thinking about something improper.

"Mind your own business." Wen Ni had clearly been stepped on her tail; she swung her fist fiercely, then gave him the back of her head and walked forward on her own.

Actually, what Wen Ni didn't say was that she wanted to ask him how he felt when he first kissed her.

But back then, they couldn't stand each other; he probably felt the same way she did—speechless just thinking about it.

There really wasn't anything worth asking.

She was already in a bad mood to begin with.

She didn't want to hear Jian Yuchen say anything she didn't want to hear.

When she pushed open the glass door and entered, the refreshing air conditioning mixed with the steaming aroma of grilled fish hit her in the face.

"Welcome! Order over here!"

An old shop wasn't as formal as a Western restaurant; the fish were chosen by the customers at the counter. Wen Ni stepped on the bright red non-slip mat, patiently picking which chubby, unlucky fellow would be eaten by her.

"How many?"

"Two." As soon as Wen Ni looked up, the landlady recognized her. "It's been a long time! I heard from your parents that you got married?"

Wen Ni felt a bit awkward. After all, the marriage was rushed, and they hadn't held a wedding banquet yet, so not many people outside knew.

Plus, having eaten late-night snacks here since high school, it felt like introducing her spouse to an elder.

"Yeah, I'm married."

The landlady looked at Jian Yuchen and nodded in admiration. "You two are a perfect match!"

She looked left and right. "There's a table by the window, but it's a bit small and close to the kitchen. Do you mind?"

It was good enough to have a table at all; what was there to be picky about?

"That's fine."

Wen Ni led Jian Yuchen over, familiar with the layout. After sitting down, she took out a tissue to wipe the table. Jian Yuchen raised an eyebrow. "It seems you're the local big shot in this area."

"That goes without saying. Don't look at whose happy home this is."

Wen Ni ordered two bottles of Wangzai milk. Jian Yuchen seemed to think it was too sweet and left it to the side without drinking it immediately.

Jian Yuchen felt that sometimes she was incredibly easy to coax, and she would just move past things on her own.

For instance, eating a pot of grilled fish now, she seemed like nothing had ever happened.

But usually at home, if he touched any of her things, she would hold a grudge for four or five days.

Jian Yuchen found it quite funny and shook his head helplessly.

"Why are you shaking your head? Is it not good!" Wen Ni’s eyes widened.

Jian Yuchen looked at the grilled fish that had just been served. "No, I was just thinking about some things."

Wen Ni breathed a sigh of relief; as long as it wasn't that the things she recommended weren't delicious, it was fine.

"Why are you in such a good mood today?" Wen Ni thought about it and felt something was wrong. Usually, Jian Yuchen would have nagged her to death, then they would have argued tooth and nail through the whole meal, and finally settled it in bed.

Jian Yuchen raised an eyebrow. "Wrongly accusing me, aren't you?"

When had he ever been bad to her? What a heartless little thing.

Wen Ni was full of suspicion. "You didn't do something to let me down, did you?"

Jian Yuchen was speechless. "You’re really asking for it."

He was trying to talk to her nicely, but she insisted on looking for trouble.

Every time Wen Ni was in a bad mood, she talked a lot, trying to shift the target.

She thought no one noticed this little habit of hers, but in fact, everyone could tell.

The grilled fish was very flavorful, not too spicy, but it didn't feel like it was just soaked in seasonings either. It had a good kick of numbness, and at this moment, the milk felt just right.

She was sweating at the tip of her nose while eating, her eyes and brows looking vivid and lively under the incandescent light.

Jian Yuchen gave her most of the fish meat and even picked out the fish bones for her.

While eating, Wen Ni reminded him, "It tastes better if you dip it in the sauce!"

Jian Yuchen watched her eat with such relish. "Should we get some crayfish too?"

Wen Ni hesitated for a moment, then pouted. "I've gained two pounds recently. I won't eat it. I'll wait until I lose some weight next time."

"I still like you a bit chubby." It felt better.

Perhaps it was the unspoken understanding between husband and wife; Wen Ni met his gaze and instantly understood what he meant.

She kicked him hard under the table. "You dirty pervert!"

"What kind of filthy language are you using in front of such cute grilled fish! It’s simply unbearable to listen to! It’s offensive to public decency! Back in the day, they would have thrown you into a pig cage."

Jian Yuchen’s eyebrows shot up, and he licked his back teeth. "I just think you look better a bit chubby now. Where did your mind go?"

"You lecher."

Wen Ni couldn't catch her breath and took a fierce bite of the fish. "Check, please! You're paying!"

Jian Yuchen found it amusing. When had he ever let her pay when she was out with him? She was acting like a miser.

"That’s 198 in total. Come back next time, and I'll give you two extra signature dishes!" the landlady greeted them warmly.

Wen Ni waved at her with a smile. As soon as she stepped out of the shop with Jian Yuchen, she seized the opportunity and jumped onto his back.

Her bag drew a heavy circle in the air and then swung back to his waist.

Jian Yuchen hooked her legs and lifted her up a bit.

Wen Ni wrapped her arms around his neck. "How is it? Am I fat now? Am I heavy?"

Jian Yuchen turned his head and glanced at her. "With your little bit of meat, I’d rather you be more active in bed and jump on my 'little brother' instead."

"I'll crush it for you." Wen Ni went to strangle his neck in annoyance.

Jian Yuchen leaned back, not angry, and clicked his tongue. "Such a vicious heart. It seems I need to use my 'Five-Thunder Bagua Whip' to properly suppress you, you little demon, so you don't go around causing trouble for everyone!"

"Oh my, you stinking Taoist, I’ve been cultivating for a thousand years, and this is the first time I’ve met someone who talks as big as you!"

Jian Yuchen walked slowly along the road. "This humble Taoist never speaks empty words. If the female benefactor doesn't believe me, why not loosen your robes and we can compare notes on the bed? We’ll see if your cultivation is deeper, or if mine is a fathom deeper still."

Wen Ni felt that with Jian Yuchen’s mouth, he could have easily swindled people out of extra copper coins back in the days when he was a traveling performer.

Once in the car, Wen Ni said, "This stretch of road is too short. You’ll have to carry me home later; I don’t want to walk."

"Easily done." He was the one taking advantage, anyway. Her little bottom wiggling against him had a charm all its own.

Wen Ni still felt she had bribed him with a delicious grilled fish, and she drove home happily.

When they reached the entrance of the residential complex, she noticed someone who looked strangely familiar. "Hmm?"

Jian Yuchen followed her gaze.

Parked across from the complex in a flashy silver sports car—wasn't that Shen Huaixu, that jerk?

"Why is he here?" Wen Ni muttered, then met Jian Yuchen’s gaze.

"Why are you looking at me like that? I have no private dealings with him."

"He still sent you flowers, didn't he?"

Oh my, the tone was so sour.

"It’s not like I asked him to."

Wen Ni said this as she turned the car into the complex.

"Why are you feeling guilty?"

"Where am I feeling guilty? How do you know he’s here for me? Who knows, maybe a friend of his lives in our complex."

Jian Yuchen didn't want to engage with her, but since a love rival had shown up at his doorstep, could he, the legitimate husband, just swallow his pride?

That would be too unlike—

chapters.title: Your affection for her is nothing more than this
chapters.content:
As soon as the car was parked in the spot, Jian Yuchen opened the door and got out.

Wen Ni saw him press the button for the lobby on the first floor. "Why are you going to the first floor? To pick up a package?"

"No, I’m going to find Shen Huaixu."

The man turned his head and gave her a sinister smile. Wen Ni shivered all over. "Why are you looking for him? What if he’s just passing by, wouldn't you be..."

Wouldn't you be making a fool of yourself?

For all they knew, he hadn't intended to look for them at all.

How embarrassing that would be.

What would he even say if he went up there?

"Isn't it obvious enough that he sent you roses? Do you really need him to spell it out?" Jian Yuchen shot her a sidelong glance and then strode out of the elevator.

"Hey!" Wen Ni never imagined such a dramatic scene would unfold.

She hurriedly chased after him. "You aren't going to beat him up, are you? He doesn't know we're married. We can just find an opportunity to explain it to him."

"Your husband is still breathing; I'm not dead yet." Should he have to taste the dung just because someone came to his door to dump it?

He wouldn't take this lying down.

Then, Jian Yuchen turned his head and pressed his hands on her shoulders, turning her in the opposite direction. "Go back."

She should interfere less in men's business.

Wen Ni was pushed back toward the elevator. Watching the man stride away without hesitation, she stomped her feet and chased after him again.

She didn't want to see a scene like in those old-fashioned idol dramas: "Stop fighting! If you want to fight, go to the dance studio!"

It was too dramatic!

Shen Huaixu was standing at the entrance, scrolling through his phone. When someone approached, he looked up and saw Jian Yuchen walking toward him.

Shen Huaixu straightened up.

Perhaps it was because, after many years, they were facing each other again.

Both men felt the other was like a lingering ghost.

"I’m not here to see you," Shen Huaixu said, his tone not particularly polite.

"I know that, of course. A man waiting for a woman in the middle of the night—I know exactly what he’s thinking." He understood the base nature of men all too well, which was exactly why he had to come find him tonight.

Shen Huaixu chuckled, then leaned against the car door and lit a cigarette. "Since I didn't end up waiting for her, what are you afraid of?"

Jian Yuchen shoved his hands into his pockets. "Since you left back then, don't come back and pester her now."

"Can't I regret it?"

"She shouldn't be your second choice. Besides, so many years have passed; coming back to entangle yourself with her is meaningless."

As he said this, Jian Yuchen’s eyes narrowed. "Do you want me to spell out why you pursued her in the first place? If you stop now, you might still leave each other with a decent impression. Do you think she’d still call you 'President Shen' if she knew the truth?"

"Shen Huaixu, when you left back then, you didn't even think of her as your girlfriend, did you?"

Wen Ni loved money, but not to the point of throwing away her self-respect and face to bow down to a man who had fooled her.

Perhaps Jian Yuchen’s words struck a hidden nerve; the man’s fingers holding the cigarette froze, letting the glowing ember burn down to his skin.

"I will compensate her."

"She doesn't need it."

Shen Huaixu sneered. "What right do you have to make decisions for her? Who are you to her?"

"At the very least, I didn't bet with a group of friends just to pursue her, only to leave without a second thought once I got her."

At this, Shen Huaixu had nothing left to say.

"This is between Wen Ni and me. What do you know?"

"I don't know anything, but I do know one thing: aside from work, I don't want you pestering her again. Roses? Save them for someone who actually wants them. Keep your hands off other people's women."

After saying this, Jian Yuchen spotted a sneaky figure near the flower bed at the entrance of the complex.

"I truly like her."

Jian Yuchen had just turned around when he heard Shen Huaixu say this.

"All these years abroad, sometimes I would miss her very much."

Jian Yuchen found it utterly ridiculous. "You didn't seem to like her that much when you were together, and you could even chat with other girls behind her back. But once you went abroad, you became a romantic saint? Why do you people always think there are eight hundred cameras filming your 'prodigal son returns' drama?"

"I don't know where this deep, ocean-like love of yours comes from, but I do know that a dog never stops eating dung."

"What you call 'liking' is just you putting a filter over those memories."

Shen Huaixu couldn't stand Jian Yuchen’s mouth. "What do you know?"

"Oh, I don't know. So, tell me, have you not been with any women since you went away all these years? Are you still a virgin?"

"..." Perhaps being asked by a love rival about his sex life was just too absurd; Shen Huaixu didn't react immediately.

But the answer was obvious.

"As you can see for yourself, your 'liking' for her is really nothing more than this."

"It’s probably just that while working together, you suddenly realized she was your high school girlfriend, thought those memories were youthful and beautiful, and decided to relive the dream. But that’s all it is, isn't it? Coming here in the middle of the night to act all sentimental—you have to see if the audience is buying it."

Jian Yuchen’s eyes were cold and indifferent. "It’s quite pathetic, Shen Huaixu."

After he finished speaking, this time he really left.

Shen Huaixu didn't leave immediately. He watched as Jian Yuchen entered the complex and started poking at something in the flower bed.

Finally, he caught a woman and tucked her under his arm, and the two of them went into the complex, bickering.

The cigarette in his hand had burned down to his knuckles.

He subconsciously flicked it away, but when he looked again, the two were already gone.

He had felt something was off during dinner.

But as for what their relationship really was, Shen Huaixu still didn't want to give up so easily.

-

"Is it fun to watch?" Jian Yuchen tucked Wen Ni under his arm, restraining her as he walked forward.

"You, you, you, let me go!" Wen Ni jumped in frustration. "My hair!"

Jian Yuchen let go, then cupped her face and ruffled her hair, leaving it a complete mess.

She was so angry she clawed at him until he finally stopped.

"What did you two say just now? Tell me and I won't give you the cold shoulder!"

Wen Ni felt she was the most magnanimous little fairy in the world! [Puffs chest out proudly]

"What? So curious? Still want to relive the old dream with him?"

"You're overthinking it. I don't eat grass I've already grazed on." Wen Ni expressed her disdain for his comment.

Jian Yuchen didn't continue to question her.

However, after they got home, Wen Ni went to the room to shower, and the man didn't squeeze in with her.

When she came out, she realized he had gone to the guest bathroom to wash up.

She pulled back the covers and got in. For the first time, the two of them lay together without wanting to do anything.

They were remarkably pure and ascetic.

Wen Ni’s head was filled with the look Wen Zhiwen had given her today; it made her feel so uncomfortable.

It was suffocating.

She rolled over twice in bed and turned to stare at Jian Yuchen.

The man was scrolling through his phone in bed; clearly, he wasn't asleep either.

The shadows on his profile made him look cold-hearted and not to be trifled with.

Wen Ni suddenly remembered the first time she saw Jian Yuchen.

He was a young man in a white shirt walking by the stairwell. As a representative of the top students, he naturally received the affection of all the teachers.

Wen Ni’s desk-mate at the time was obsessed with him.

Wherever she went, she would drag Wen Ni along and nudge her, "Jian Yuchen, Jian Yuchen, did he look at me?"

"Did he walk past?"

It made Wen Ni feel like she had a radar on her head for a while; whenever she heard the name Jian Yuchen, she would subconsciously look toward him.

chapters.title: You obviously can't hold back when you see a fairy like me
chapters.content:
Back then, Jian Yuchen was indeed a golden child.

He reported to school a month after the semester started, and in his first monthly exam, he ranked first in the entire grade, breaking all previous records.

For a while, everyone was discussing him wherever they went.

They said the principal had personally gone to another school to dig him up, taking advantage of the summer break to make him one of their own.

They made an exception for him: he was a day student who lived directly in the complex across from the school.

It made Wen Ni, who lived in the dorms, so envious and jealous that she felt like crawling into a dark hole.

Originally, Jian Yuchen and someone like her, who ranked outside the top 20 in the grade, wouldn't have had any intersection.

But as it happened, he was in the class next to hers.

Several times, when Wen Ni was caught eating in class or was punished by standing outside for being late, she would run into Jian Yuchen passing by.

Especially when she felt Jian Yuchen’s gaze land on her, Wen Ni felt her pure, maidenly heart shatter into pieces.

That was when she suddenly started disliking him.

He must have been laughing at her behind her back.

She didn't want to have anything to do with him.

Wen Ni thought back to the past and sighed silently.

How did she end up becoming his wife?

The man’s voice came through. "What’s the matter? Sighing because you didn't get to talk to him?"

Look at that sour, jealous husband act.

Wen Ni hugged her little quilt tight, turned her head, and poked Jian Yuchen’s arm with her finger.

The hell was this dog of a man doing at the gym to get arms like that? He poked her, and it hurt her nails.

Wen Ni silently tried to pull her finger back, but it was seized by a large hand.

"If you have something to say, say it."

"Let’s get one thing straight: if you want to go down there to have a secret rendezvous with your first love, you’ll have to do it over my dead body." Jian Yuchen’s long, narrow eyes lowered, staring fixedly at Wen Ni.

It was as if he would lunge over and bite her throat out if her next sentence was that she really intended to go down there.

Wen Ni blinked. "I was just wondering how we ended up as a married couple. Don't you find it incredible?"

From the mutual loathing in high school, to the icy coldness in college, to the shouting matches between their companies during business collaborations.

And then, just like that, they were married.

She recalled her desk mate, who used to sleep on the bunk above her, sighing about how she wanted to marry Jian Yuchen and never be apart from him.

Wen Ni felt that she had stumbled upon this wish without even trying, and wondered if the Old Man Under the Moon had tied the red strings wrong.

To Jian Yuchen, this remark meant only one thing.

"If you don't want to be married to me, who do you want to be with? Shen Huaixu?"

"Too late! You’re already on my spouse line."

Wen Ni felt her temper was good enough today; she didn't get angry at his words. Instead, she giggled and leaned in to wrap her arms around his waist, clearly feeling the man’s breathing hitch.

"Hey, back then, why did you agree to marry me?"

Actually, they were both very young at the time.

They hadn't been graduated for long.

The height of summer at age 24.

Carrying the impulsive energy of someone just entering society, they hadn't expected to be pressured into marriage by their elders.

It wasn't the first time Wen Zhiwen had told her to get married early.

Wen Ni had never taken it seriously.

Until one day, she came home to find the living room full of people—a strange man, his parents, and even a so-called matchmaker.

Only then did Wen Ni feel offended.

Wen Zhiwen was clearly very satisfied with this arrangement.

When Wen Ni rejected the man that evening, Wen Zhiwen angrily demanded to know what exactly she was dissatisfied with.

Why should she be satisfied?

This wasn't an arranged marriage from ancient times; if he was so satisfied, why didn't he go marry the guy himself?

"You just graduated at 23, your job isn't stable, and I haven't said anything. Now you refuse to take the civil service exam and insist on being an interior designer at some renovation company. Fine! Let’s see what kind of person you can find. You’ll regret it sooner or later. I’m telling you, if you aren't married by 25 and continue to embarrass me, I don't want you as my daughter anymore."

Wen Ni thought it was absolutely absurd.

In high school, when he found a love letter in her bag, he wanted to beat her to death; the moment she graduated college, he couldn't wait for her to give him a fat grandson.

She couldn't remember which blind date that was.

She was already annoyed from drawing blueprints, and having rushed over from the construction site, she appeared in the private room looking disheveled. The result was obvious: she was severely scolded by Wen Zhiwen, who practically wanted to disown her on the spot.

Wen Ni naturally had a huge fight with him.

But as long as she couldn't legally sever the father-daughter relationship, she knew the next blind date was probably already in the works.

She took a cigarette from her bag and stood by the flower bed of the restaurant, smoking one after another.

She didn't care how passersby looked at her.

She noticed Jian Yuchen when he suddenly walked up to her. "Got a light?"

Wen Ni looked up, her eyeliner smeared at the corners of her eyes. Jian Yuchen thought she looked like a depressed female ghost at that moment.

But Wen Ni was in a bad mood and naturally didn't want to lend him one.

"No lighter."

"Then how did you light your cigarette?"

"I used my 'Samadhi True Fire,' okay?"

Jian Yuchen let out a scoff. Before Wen Ni could react, she felt the man lean down, and he lit his cigarette off the tip of hers—that was how he "borrowed" the light.

His thin eyelids drooped, his lashes long but not curled, looking down at her vertically. His eyes held that same calm, dead look as always.

He was so close that Wen Ni could smell the woody base notes on him, lingering like the scent of grass and trees after a rain.

Wen Ni suddenly said, as if possessed: "Do you want to marry me?"

Jian Yuchen only raised his eyes slightly at the words. Just as Wen Ni was about to say she was joking, the man spoke: "Sure. Get the certificate tomorrow?"

?

And then Wen Ni was dragged upstairs by Jian Yuchen to meet his parents.

Only then did Wen Ni realize he had been having dinner with them, and they just happened to get the matter done.

Jian Yuchen’s parents didn't look much like him; they looked like intellectuals. She couldn't figure out how two such polite and gentle people had produced such a sharp-tongued, mean-spirited son.

Wen Ni had been in a "let it all rot" mindset at the time, so she went home and told Wen Zhiwen that she was bringing her boyfriend and his whole family over the next day to discuss marriage.

Wen Zhiwen was so angry he wanted to kill her on the spot.

The next day, nothing was prepared at home, but to her surprise, Jian Yuchen’s family really came.

As it turned out, Wen Zhiwen actually knew them, calling the father "old brother" repeatedly.

They had known each other back when they were cadres in college, but the other man had risen through the ranks, while Wen Zhiwen, thanks to his rotten temper and lack of emotional intelligence, was still spinning his wheels at his original unit.

Jian Yuchen had been the "neighbor's kid" since he was small.

Wen Zhiwen had nothing to say about this future son-in-law; if his age hadn't prevented it, Wen Ni suspected he would have wanted to be the bride himself.

The wedding went more smoothly than even Wen Ni had expected.

By the time she held the household registration book and went to get the certificate, Wen Ni still hadn't come to her senses.

She had actually married Jian Yuchen.

And he was the "Party A" client of her company.

As for how he later became a partner, that was a different story.

At the very least, whenever Wen Ni thought about it now, she found it incredible.

"Were you also being pressured to marry back then, and since I—a clever, cute, and brilliant little fairy—appeared before you, you couldn't help but go along with it?"

chapters.title: Who is the Supporting Character?
chapters.content:
Jian Yuchen finally put down what he was holding, turned his head, lifted the quilt, and pulled up her dress.

Before Wen Ni could recover, the man had already pressed down, his voice low and hoarse. "Yeah, I really couldn't help it."

"Hey, I'm talking to you about something serious!" Wen Ni reached out to block his wandering hands.

But her blocking technique was practically non-existent.

Jian Yuchen treated it all as marital play.

"Is marital intimacy not a serious matter?" The man raised an eyebrow, tossing two thin pieces of fabric out from under the covers.

Wen Ni eventually became muddled and lost her focus...

In the man's repeated contributions, she was forced, helpless, to answer his questions.

"Who are you thinking about?"

"Thinking about you."

He seemed quite satisfied with this answer, so he stopped being so aggressive.

"Like me that much?"

This was probably the first time he had said this line, so after saying it, he was uncharacteristically expectant of her answer.

But Wen Ni was always Wen Ni; she could be incredibly dense in some aspects.

Her gaze landed on Jian Yuchen’s face. "Pfft—in your dreams. I was thinking about our wedding night."

"Hmm, tonight's position is indeed quite similar. You were so shy back then, wouldn't even let me look after you were stripped bare. So pretentious."

Then the man didn't give her any more time to talk back; after all, they were already on his battlefield, and he didn't want to hear anything he didn't like coming out of her chattering little mouth.

Wen Ni really wanted to reminisce about that time with him, but the man didn't seem to care.

When it was over, she was drenched in sweat. She was carried to the bathroom to be washed, and she fell asleep, drowsy, on his shoulder.

Before falling asleep, she felt him carefully and meticulously applying ointment to her.

She even heard a frustrated, "It's chafed."

Wen Ni was exhausted. She tried to lift her eyelids for a moment, but couldn't, and drifted straight off to sleep.

Wen Ni dreamed of the past. Since she had been thinking about it before bed, it was only natural that she would dream of it.

That first kiss.

In the school drama club.

She had been "conscripted" at the time, dragged in by the arts committee member to fill a spot, playing the witch who persecuted the princess.

Wen Ni held that red apple, wanting to take a bite several times.

She sat in the corner of the backstage, yawning out of boredom.

After all, her lines were so few that she didn't need to keep memorizing them.

With a black cloak draped over her, no one could tell the difference between her and the queen.

Wen Ni felt that by today's standards, she was just a body double.

She only needed to stand in the rehearsed position and complete the task.

The drama club wasn't very popular; compared to the street dance club and the cheerleading squad, no one appreciated it here at all.

Still, Wen Ni was very professional, upholding the principle of "I am a tree," sitting there motionless.

Until she heard a scoff.

Wen Ni turned around but didn't see anyone, because the hood of the black cloak blocked most of her view.

She pulled it back and saw Jian Yuchen in a white shirt.

For a long time, he was the trendsetter for white shirts at school. After all, in junior high and high school, most people were quite sloppy, wearing school uniforms all day without any sense of style, tortured by test papers and homework until they looked like zombies.

But whenever he appeared, his style was the opposite of everyone else's—clean and crisp.

So, for a while, many boys tried to copy Jian Yuchen’s style, but the results were... well, unsatisfactory.

As her desk mate put it, he was the protagonist who walked out of a novel, and the rest were just background extras.

Out of a sense of rivalry, Wen Ni vehemently refuted this, emphasizing that Shen Huaixu looked more like a protagonist, while Jian Yuchen was the type of "second male lead" who would never get the girl.

Unfortunately for her, Jian Yuchen happened to overhear this.

From then on, the grudge between the two deepened for no reason.

For instance, his scoff right now made Wen Ni feel as if he were mocking her: *Look, in reality, you’re the villain, and I’m the protagonist.*

This made Wen Ni unable to sit still. "Why are you sneaking around behind me without making a sound? Trying to ambush me?"

Jian Yuchen looked down at her. "I saw someone trying to eat the props, so I’m just speaking up for justice under normal circumstances."

See? He even emphasized "justice."

Wen Ni shook her cloak. "Why are you here? I thought you went to the basketball club. Didn't you join the team last month to win glory for the school?"

She heard he played quite well and had gained a group of fangirls from outside the school.

"Sounds like you care about me quite a bit." Jian Yuchen leaned against the side, his gaze fixed on the stage, though he was speaking to her.

Wen Ni jumped like a cat whose tail had been stepped on. "Stop talking nonsense! Who cares about you! Narcissist!"

On stage, the princess and the seven dwarfs were reciting their lines. Just as they reached the climax, the whole room went silent because of Wen Ni’s shout.

After realizing what was happening, Wen Ni quickly shrank behind Jian Yuchen.

However, everyone's attention was quickly drawn to Jian Yuchen's arrival.

"Jian Yuchen!"

"Great job, club president! You brought us the class heartthrob!"

"Now we don't have to worry about viewers! This show has to pass censorship!"

Wen Ni subconsciously rolled her eyes. See, the Jian Yuchen effect.

The prince's scenes weren't actually that many; Jian Yuchen and Wen Ni spent most of their time backstage waiting for their scenes.

During the second period of evening self-study in the second year of high school, Wen Ni would bump into Jian Yuchen as soon as she left the classroom for the auditorium, and the two would walk together.

At this time, the school was quiet, and they walked one after the other.

There was a shortcut between the teaching building and the auditorium, passing through flowerbeds and green belts.

An English corner had even been set up there.

During the day, the falling petals were quite beautiful. The night air became somewhat eerie and terrifying.

Especially when the night wind picked up, Wen Ni could only shuffle slowly closer to Jian Yuchen, lest he walk too fast and leave her behind.

"Are you afraid of ghosts?" Most of the time, Jian Yuchen didn't talk to her.

So his sudden question that day was like a special effect in a horror movie for the easily startled Wen Ni.

She wanted to grab onto something for a sense of security, but there was nothing to hold onto.

Until Jian Yuchen reached out his hand, "Hold on tight."

Wen Ni stared at his clean hand, not moving for a long time.

Until Jian Yuchen said impatiently, "Never mind then."

Just as he was about to pull away, Wen Ni pinched his middle finger between two fingertips.

Clearly, after oscillating between her unyielding spirit and her fear of death, she decided to retain seven or eight parts of her dignity while abandoning some of her dislike for Jian Yuchen.

So she held up two fingers, seeking just a tiny bit of security! It wasn't excessive.

Any more, and there wouldn't be any left.

Jian Yuchen probably hadn't expected her to have this tactic, and couldn't help but turn and smile.

"What are you laughing at!"

"You were the one who held out your hand, I... I was just being polite." Wen Ni stood awkwardly beside him. "Hurry up and go, we're waiting for the two of us."

Because it wasn't a major scene, they always arrived last.

chapters.title: Prince and Witch
chapters.content:
Even though he was the one who held out his hand first, it ended up with Wen Ni walking forward with her head down.

The evening breeze carried the fresh scent of citrus in the air.

Wen Ni recognized it immediately as the principal's most prized orange tree.

It was said to have been planted during a plant festival one year, and only the principal's tree bore fruit, making it his most cherished possession. A special school anniversary was established for the day it bore fruit.

To prevent students from picking all the bark off the orange trees, a fence was erected, prohibiting anyone from approaching within a two-meter radius.

Looking back now, Wen Ni didn't find it bad.

At least her first time holding hands with Jian Yuchen had some pleasant memories.

However, when they reached the vicinity of the auditorium, standing under a streetlamp, she released his hand with lightning speed and walked on her own.

Under the streetlamp, the ends of her hair almost flew into the air.

The air particles danced in the light, also causing the hem of her knee-length skirt to flutter.

The heavy doors of the auditorium opened.

"You two are finally here! The script has been changed!"

Jian Yuchen's addition increased the drama, and the Literature and Art Department, for Jian Yuchen's many female admirers, directly changed the script so that the prince would appear earlier.

Wen Ni and Fan Yanwen, the sports committee member who played the villain, became the two main antagonists in this drama.

Fan Yanwen was quite happy, after all, he had a few more minutes of action scenes. He even tied a bright bow tie on the dinosaur costume he bought online.

Wen Ni wanted to tell him that nobody cares whether a dinosaur wears a bow tie, a bow tie, or a knot.

It's just a dinosaur! You don't even need to show your face.

Clearly, Fan Yanwen was very dissatisfied with Wen Ni's passive-aggressive attitude.

Therefore, for the next half hour of rehearsals, Fan Yanwen took every opportunity to brainwash her.

"Do what you love. Even minor characters like us have our day!"

"..."

Thanks, I don't want to be in the spotlight.

When she saw the newly revised script and the club president's smug, praise-awaiting expression,

Wen Ni rolled her eyes to the sky. Why should she, a queen's stand-in, fight to the death with the prince for an apple! "Can't you at least respect the original fans?!"

However, as a villain, she never really had a voice.

Besides, she was just a stand-in for the vicious female supporting character.

On the day of the actual performance, Wen Ni quickly donned her black cloak, clutching her little apple, and sat backstage, closing her eyes to rest.

If she could just get through this night smoothly, Wen Ni could retire successfully, continue reading shoujo manga in her evening study hall, and live happily ever after with her paper-doll husband.

However, fate was unkind. Wen Ni knew that anything involving Jian Yuchen wouldn't go too smoothly.

A handsome and brave prince kissing a pure and beautiful princess awake, what a sacred and beautiful classic scene!

Wen Ni really wanted to open the club president's brain and see why she was assigned this scene that interrupted the main characters' intimacy.

"Haven't you always wanted to find an opportunity to stab Jian Yuchen in the back? Go for it, Wen Ni! Playing yourself is the best way to showcase your acting skills. This will be a pivotal moment in your life, a turning point in your career! Having you in our drama club is a blessing!"

Then, Wen Ni was abruptly pushed onto the stage by the club president. Her cape was too long, and she stepped on it, stumbling a few steps as she came out.

Wen Ni listened to the club president's excited little voice through her earpiece, "Look, those few stumbles she took on her entrance were so realistic!"

"..."

You guys are my bad luck.

The audience was silent. The entire school was there, oh, and perhaps their parents too.

Of course, Wen Zhiwen might be there, sitting in some corner, staring at her with a judgmental gaze.

Wen Ni suddenly didn't know what to do with her hands and feet. When she reached Jian Yuchen, she was even blinded by the stage lights.

The voice in the earpiece continued.

"She seems to be moving her arms and legs in unison. Is she too nervous?"

"No way, she was fine during rehearsals."

Wen Ni became even more nervous from their comments.

Did I mess up?!

She even forgot her lines, stammering and unable to utter a single word.

Fan Yanwen and she had already developed a strong bond backstage.

Seeing that Wen Ni was about to mess up, he suddenly jumped out.

"Dak-dala-gu-dada-gulu-lu Prince! You stole my little princess! Let me kiss her awake!"

This completely unpredictable new version of Snow White obviously caused an uproar among the teachers and students.

Wen Ni guessed they were probably shocked that the prince's name was so awful, and that in good families, the prince wielded a peach wood sword and a talisman when fighting a dragon!

But at that moment, she desperately wanted to kneel down before Fan Yanwen!

Brother, you're my brother! My dear brother! All attention was drawn to Fan Yanwen, and Wen Ni, at that moment, wanted to snatch the prince's sword.

But just as she reached out, Fan Yanwen, perhaps in a frenzy, swung his massive tail with a powerful thud, slamming Jian Yuchen, who was standing there, right into his arms.

As that face drew closer and closer, Wen Ni was knocked to the ground by Jian Yuchen.

The entire audience gaped in stunned silence.

The prince kissed the witch.

What did that feel like?

His lips weren't as hard as when he was cursing.

They were soft, and she could hear a muffled groan as they pressed against each other.

At that moment, Wen Ni was certain they both held their breath, their faces flushed, staring at each other helplessly.

This unexpected turn of events was far too much for them, who were still relatively innocent at the time.

Wen Ni even imagined her future high school life; she would be locked in a life-or-death struggle with Jian Yuchen.

She clearly heard the sound of her braces snapping; the wire was rapidly piercing through the soft flesh of her mouth, breaking free of its original track.

A strange, indescribable electric current surged through her body.

Wen Ni had forgotten how she was carried off the stage by Jian Yuchen, looking completely dazed.

She only remembered that his lip was bleeding, while hers was even worse.

Because of this accident, she unexpectedly won the Most Popular Award, and she also received a Best Couple Award with Jian Yuchen.

The price was her braces, which she had only had for two days.

But in her dream, Jian Yuchen didn't leave. He held the back of her head and deepened the kiss.

His hand even somewhat improperly opened her black cloak.

Wen Ni was startled, but uncontrollably followed his rhythm.

Jian Yuchen, who was half-asleep and suddenly embraced tightly by Wen Ni: ?

He looked down at his little wife in his arms, wondering what she was dreaming about.

"No, they're all watching."

"Hmm~ Be gentle, ouch, it itches here."

"Fan Yanwen, take the princess away!"

"No, Jian Yuchen, no!"

...

What kind of dream is this?

It sounds a bit suggestive, but why is Fan Yanwen involved?!

chapters.title: This Old Lady’s Plenty Experienced
chapters.content:
Wen Ni felt short of breath and suddenly opened her mouth wide to breathe, only to be jolted awake.

When she opened her eyes and saw the man's probing yet disgusted gaze,

she felt as if a bucket of cold water had been poured over her head.

"Wh...what are you doing?" She guiltily looked away. Jian Yuchen looked her up and down, then tugged at a strand of her hair and asked, "What naughty things were you doing in your dream?"

Wen Ni felt like she'd been stepped on. "What naughty things!"

"Ugh~ You always lie so loudly, you want me to imitate you, right?"

Then Wen Ni saw Jian Yuchen, expressionless, pinching his throat and humming incoherently, mimicking her tone, "Jian Yuchen~, no~"

"No what?" He suddenly stopped, asking coldly.

Wen Ni's eyes darted to the left. "I told you not to add celery, I already said I don't like celery."

"Do you use this tone with celery, too?"

Jian Yuchen tilted his head slightly, then wore an expression of disgust. "I never expected you to be such a pervert."

Wen Ni thrashed about under the covers. "Who—who’s the pervert? It’s your own mind that’s dirty; you see and hear filth in everything!"

"Don't assume everyone else is like you."

Jian Yuchen rolled his tongue in his mouth, making a crisp clicking sound. "Oh, my mind is dirty? In that case, you wouldn't mind if I used that audio as my alarm tone, would you?"

"You dare?!" Wen Ni was furious. How could this man manage to record audio anytime, anywhere?!

*Aaaaaah, I’m going to kill you!*
